title: Been working on something... For #aiGameDev little ones :)
author: orblabs
selftext:
Very close to releasing (Open Source) Greia, a project that was born and developed for my daughters but that thanks to a very warm reception on reddit has received months of polish so to be usable by other parents.  
The core concept of Greia was that of creating an extremely lightweight linux distro that could run on early 2000s potatoes as i had a few lying around, and it should ALL be, from boot to shut off, very little kid friendly, no complex desktops, no task bars, no keys that if pressed will eject the kid from the experience, no way for the kids to get on youtube and other stuff.  
And... the vibecoding part, a set of skills and tools for LLM agents so that parents can easily ask their agent "Make a new game for my daughter, she is fixating on trains, make it fun and somewhat educational". The agent will deliver an "app" (we call them "activities" in Greia) that is graphically consistent with the rest of the system, uses a common UI and design language (core UI always in same place etc), ties to system wide achievements etc, is localized in one or multiple languages AND records voices with the systems characters voices for all interactions (3 or 4 years old can't really read).  
Among the concepts there is that the kids receive a polished and clean experience their parents can control and vet, no internet access, no ads, no confusion.   
Parents receive tools and instructions for their agents to expand Greia making it tailored for their kids focusing on their current passions, what they should be learning or just some plain simple gaming. 

There is much more, but thought i should start teasing some.... Full release will hopefully happen this coming week.

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body:
But why would I want my child to spend more time on the display. I want to reduce that. Does it have parental settings? 

Looking good. Good luck

replies.author: orblabs
replies.body:
Thanks ! It has an app for parents to set users, screen time and even what activities are visible on certain days / time if a parent wants (so for example a kid could focus on math on mondays, reading / writing on Thursdays or whatever combination.  
I am fine with my girls spending some time on a screen i just don’t want them to watch YouTube or general cartoons slop. Now they have some cute games that has them play and learn something and can add stuff as they get interested in other stuff (for example a couple of months ago we watched free Willy and they got fixated on orcas, the day after they had a “game” where they could per and play with orcas and learn facts about them)
